records.name: St. Cyprian Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at Cobbs Creek Parkway and Cedar Avenue in West Philadelphia. Its ministries include religious education, a food pantry and clothes room, and a Bible study. It also offers an African French Mass on Sunday afternoons.
records.what_you_do: Come to a Sunday Mass: English at 8 am or 11 am, Nigerian at 1 pm, or African French at 3:30 pm. Ask the office about joining a ministry, such as greeting, the choir, religious education, or the food pantry and clothes room.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8 am and 11 am in English, a Nigerian Mass at 1 pm, and an African French Mass at 3:30 pm. Weekday Mass at 8 am. Holy days at 7 am and 7 pm. Confessions 15 minutes before Mass or by appointment.

locations.label: Parish church
locations.address: Cobbs Creek Pkwy. and Cedar Ave.

access.notes: The 11 am Sunday Mass and daily Mass can be viewed on the parish's YouTube page.

first_step.how: Come to the 11 am Sunday Mass, then email or call the parish office between 8 am and 3 pm on weekdays to ask about joining a ministry.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the contact page lists office hours, a phone line and an email. The site does not describe a newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, so you can come and sit. The parish lists ministries for greeting, hospitality and outreach, and the office can point you to the one that fits. The Nigerian and African French Masses are on Sunday afternoons if you want a Mass in another language.
first_visit_tips: Call or email the office first: it is open 8 am to 3 pm, and evening visits are by appointment.

records.notes: Ministries page lists 3 categories and 27 names with no descriptions. The tier 1 chaplaincy wording is supported only by the African French Mass at 3:30 pm on Sundays, so the summary names that Mass instead. Tier 1 gave the rectory as 525 Cobbs Creek Pkwy.; the contact page gives the office as 525 S. 63rd St., which is used here. The upcoming events page returned 404. The bulletin file path suggests October 2026, but the page has no written date, so it is not used as evidence. Fetches: 5 of 6.

records.name: St. Dominic Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on Frankford Avenue in the Northeast with weekend Masses, a chapel open for adoration most days, and a Saturday Miraculous Medal novena.
records.what_you_do: Come to a weekend Mass, pray in the adoration chapel, or join the Saturday Miraculous Medal novena after the 9 am Mass. To join the parish, fill in the online registration form on the site or call the office at 215-624-5502.

schedule.text: Saturday Masses at 9 am and 4:30 pm. Sunday Masses at 8:30 am and 10:30 am. Weekday Mass at 8 am in the chapel. Holy days at 8 am and 7 pm. Confessions Saturdays 3:30 to 4 pm or by appointment. The adoration chapel is open daily 8 am to 7 pm except during Mass times, and it is closed after the last Sunday Mass.

cost.text: Mass and adoration are free to attend.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass, then fill in the online registration form on the site or call the office at 215-624-5502 to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: Mass and adoration are open to anyone, and the site has a registration form and office hours. No newcomer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, so you can come, sit and leave. The adoration chapel is open for quiet prayer most days, but it closes during Mass times and after the last Sunday Mass. The registration form asks for household details, and the site sends it by email.
first_visit_tips: The office is open 9 am to 5 pm on weekdays and by appointment on Saturday, so call before you come by.
Check the adoration hours first, since the chapel is closed during Mass times and after the last Sunday Mass.

records.notes: The groups page lists no parish groups. The events and mass-schedule pages returned 404 at guessed addresses. Church bulletins are PDFs with no visible date, so no sign-of-life date is set. Tier 1 had holy days at 12:05 pm; the homepage says 8 am and 7 pm, which is used. Fetches: 6 of 6.

records.name: St. Francis de Sales Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 47th Street and Springfield Avenue in West Philadelphia with Sunday Masses, a Saturday evening Vigil, and weekday morning Mass.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or join a parish group: altar servers, the parish choir, liturgical ministers, reading groups, the Legion of Mary (weekly after the 10:15 am Mass in the lower church), or Family Faith Formation for parents who teach their children. Call the rectory at 215-222-5819 to ask how to join.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 7 am and 10:15 am, with the 10:15 Mass as the main Mass, sung with choir and organ. Saturday vigil Mass at 5 pm. Weekday Mass at 7 am Monday to Friday. Saturday and national holiday Mass at 8:30 am. Confession Saturdays 9 to 10 am and Sundays 9:30 to 10 am, or by appointment.

locations.label: Rectory (church at 47th St. and Springfield Ave.)

first_step.how: Come to the 10:15 am Sunday Mass, then call the rectory at 215-222-5819 to ask about a parish group or about becoming a member.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone. The site says to call the rectory to become a member and offers Flocknote email updates. No newcomer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. The 10:15 am Sunday Mass is the main one, with choir and organ. If you are not yet Catholic, or you are coming back to the Church, the rectory can tell you about the adult catechism sessions.
first_visit_tips: Call the rectory at 215-222-5819 with questions about groups or membership, since the site lists no office hours.
Sign up for Flocknote email updates on the site if you want parish news.

records.notes: The Mass times page gives Saturday confession at 9 to 10 am; tier 1 had 4:15 to 4:45 pm, and the site's version is used. The only dated item on the site is a Saturday and holiday Mass time change dated May 1, 2023. Probably_active rests on a standing schedule and an undated site, so a reviewer may judge it dormant under the 24 month rule. Coordinator names and emails on the organizations page are not copied; the rectory line is used instead. The Family Faith Formation page returned 404 at a guessed address. Fetches: 6 of 6.

records.name: St. Helena Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish near Fifth Street and Godfrey Avenue with Masses in English, Vietnamese and Spanish.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in English, Vietnamese or Spanish. The parish lists ministries you can join, including lector, usher, choir, guitar group, catechist for grades 1 to 8, food bank volunteer, and volunteer cook for homebound neighbors. Adults who are not yet Catholic can call the rectory about the RCIA sessions.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 4:30 pm. Sunday Masses at 8 am, 9:30 am (Vietnamese), 11:15 am and 12:30 pm (Spanish). Weekday Mass at 8 am Monday to Saturday. First Fridays at 8 am and 7 pm. Holy days at 8 am and 9 am, plus a 7 pm Mass in three languages. Saturday confession 4 to 4:30 pm.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass (8 am, 9:30 am in Vietnamese, 11:15 am, or 12:30 pm in Spanish), then call the office at 215-424-1300 to ask about a ministry or the RCIA sessions.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone. The site lists a phone line and an email, and the ministries page says to contact the parish to join. No newcomer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free, and it is offered in English, Vietnamese and Spanish, so you can pick the time that fits your language. A guitar group plays at the 11:15 am Mass twice a month. The rectory is open 9 am to 5 pm on weekdays, closed noon to 1 pm, if you want to ask about joining.
first_visit_tips: Rectory hours are Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, closed noon to 1 pm, so call before you come by.

records.notes: The newcomers page returned 404 at two guessed addresses, so newcomer steps come from the rectory line, the ministries page and the RCIA page. The food bank site (sthoc.wordpress.com) is private and was not read, so it is listed under blocked. Caring for Friends (volunteer cooks) is listed as a lead. The parish council and finance committee meet on alternating second Tuesdays at 7 pm and are not added. Fetches: 5 of 6.

records.name: St. Ignatius of Loyola Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish near 43rd and Wallace Streets in West Philadelphia with a 10 am Sunday Mass and a Tuesday food pantry for people who live in the 19104 zip code.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Sunday 10 am Mass. Children can join PREP on Sundays after Mass, or sacramental preparation on Saturday mornings, through the religious education office. People who live in the 19104 zip code can apply to the Tuesday food pantry at 636 N. 43rd St., and should bring identification.

schedule.text: Sunday Mass at 10 am. Weekday Mass on the first Wednesday of the month at 9:30 am at West Park Nursing Home. Holy days at 10 am and 7 pm. Reconciliation before Sunday Mass, 9:15 to 9:45 am, or by appointment. The food pantry committee meets Tuesdays 10 am to noon, and the pantry is closed on holidays and the fifth Tuesday of the month.

locations.label: Weekday Mass (first Wednesday, West Park Nursing Home)

first_step.how: Come to the Sunday 10 am Mass at the church at 43rd and Wallace Streets. To ask about religious education or the food pantry, call the parish at 215-386-5065.
first_step.basis: Sunday Mass is open to anyone. The site has a register option and a phone line, and the food pantry page explains how to apply. No newcomer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, so you can come and sit. For food help, the pantry asks you to show identification and apply before you get a bag of groceries, and pickups happen once a month. Children's religious education meets on Sundays after Mass for PREP, with Saturday morning classes for sacramental preparation.
first_visit_tips: Bring identification if you are applying for food help.
The parish office is open 9 am to 4 pm, Monday to Thursday, and closed on Fridays.

records.notes: Tier 1 had Sunday confession at 7:45 to 8:45 am and weekday Mass Monday to Friday in the nursing home chapel. The parish homepage now says reconciliation is 9:15 to 9:45 am before Sunday Mass and weekday Mass is on the first Wednesday only, so the site's version is used. The food cupboard claim from the Archdiocese day of service list is replaced by the parish's own food pantry page. That page says people 55 and older can get an extra senior box on the third Tuesday, and that the pantry serves residents of zip 19104. The West Park Nursing Home address is from tier 1 and does not appear on the parish site. The news and mass-times pages returned 404. The 2026 dated items come from the homepage: a September 20, 2026 pastor's note and October 2026 events. Fetches: 6 of 6.

records.name: St. Jerome Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at Holme Avenue and Stamford Street in Northeast Philadelphia with several Sunday Masses, a Saturday vigil, and weekday Mass at 8 am.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday Mass or the Saturday vigil. Children can join PREP, the parish religious education program, and the 9:30 am Sunday Mass has a Children's Liturgy of the Word. Adults who are becoming Catholic can ask about OCIA. The site also lists a food assistance phone line at 215-805-8479.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 7:30 am, 9:30 am (with Children's Liturgy of the Word) and 11 am, according to the parish website. An Archdiocese listing also shows 6:30 am and 8 am, so call to confirm. Saturday vigil at 4:30 pm. Weekday Mass at 8 am Monday to Friday. Holy days at 8 am, 10 am, 12 pm and 7 pm. Confessions Saturdays 3:30 to 4:15 pm. The church is open for private prayer 9 am to noon daily except Saturday.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass, then call the parish office at 215-333-4461 to ask how to register or about PREP or OCIA.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the office phone is listed. The site has a 'Register with us' page, which we could not open. No newcomer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, so you can come and sit. The 9:30 am Sunday Mass has a Children's Liturgy of the Word for younger children. The church is also open for quiet prayer from 9 am to noon, daily except Saturday.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-333-4461 to confirm Sunday times, because the parish site and the Archdiocese listing do not match.
Confessions are on Saturdays from 3:30 to 4:15 pm.

records.notes: Sunday Mass times conflict. The parish homepage lists 7:30 am, 9:30 am (Children's Liturgy) and 11 am. The Archdiocese page lists 6:30, 8, 9:30 and 11 am; I read that through a web search summary and did not open the page. Tier 1 had the Archdiocese version, so both are stated and the site's version leads, with a call-to-confirm line. The register, events, and mass-times pages returned 404 at guessed addresses. The site's only written date is a 2023 copyright line, which is not used. The site names a 'Saint Jerome Memorial Society' as its one group-like item; it is listed as a lead. Fetches: 6 of 6. WebSearch: 1 of 1.

records.name: St. John Cantius Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish with Sunday Masses at 8, 10 and 11:30 am, some Masses said in Polish, and a Saturday evening vigil.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, and ask which Masses are in Polish. The parish lists about 17 ministries and groups, including greeters, ushers, lectors, altar servers, a boys' Scout troop on Tuesday evenings at 7 pm, senior groups, and Aid for Friends, which cooks and delivers meals for homebound and older neighbors. For children and adults preparing for the sacraments, call the parish office at 215-535-6667.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8 am (quiet, with no organ music), 10 am (with organ music) and 11:30 am (in Polish). Saturday vigil at 4:30 pm. Weekday Mass at 8 am Monday to Friday, and at 8 am on Saturday in Polish. First Friday Mass at 7 pm in Polish. Confessions Saturdays 3:30 to 4:15 pm, before the vigil or by appointment. Eucharistic exposition Wednesdays 4 to 7 pm from October to June, with a Polish rosary at 6:30 pm.

access.notes: The 8 am Sunday Mass is a quiet Mass with no organ music, as the site describes it.

first_step.how: Come to the 10 am Sunday Mass in English or the 11:30 am Mass in Polish, then call the parish office at 215-535-6667 to ask about the Scouts, the senior groups, or the faith formation classes.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the parish lists a phone line and a ministries page that says to call to join. No newcomer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free to attend, and you can come and sit without signing up. The 8 am Sunday Mass is quiet with no organ music, and the 10 am Mass has organ music. The 11:30 am Mass is in Polish.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-535-6667 to confirm times, because a parish notice says some Mass times differ from the website.
Confessions are on Saturdays from 3:30 to 4:15 pm, before the vigil Mass or by appointment.

records.notes: The ministries page lists 17 groups; none is a Polish community group, and it gives no meeting times except the Scouts. The religious education page gives no ages, times or fees and points to the parish office. The parish office email is hidden behind a protection notice, so no email is listed. The registration, PREP, and Mass schedule pages returned 404 at guessed addresses. The newest dated item is a 40 Hours Devotion on October 18 to 20, 2026. A parish bingo notice with no year is not used. This record used 7 fetches, one over the six per group limit; no further fetches were made for this group.

leads_only.name: Saint Jerome Memorial Society
leads_only.note: Named on the parish site as its one group-like item. No own website is named, so not checked.

leads_only.name: Caring for Friends
leads_only.note: Named on the St. Helena ministries page as the partner for volunteer meal cooks. No own website is given, so not checked.

blocked.note: St. Helena food bank site. It is a private WordPress site that asks visitors to log in to request access, so it was not read. Food bank hours, address and eligibility are unknown.

notes: All seven are Catholic parishes that passed tier 1. All seven are publish. None is defunct or out of scope. Fetches: 42 in total, 41 on the seven parish sites and 1 on a lead site. St. John Cantius took 7 fetches, one over the six per group limit, and no more were made for it. WebSearch: 1 of 1 used, on St. Jerome's Sunday Mass times. Many guessed page addresses returned 404; each is noted in its record. Tier 1 times and addresses were corrected from the parish sites where they disagreed: St. Dominic holy days, St. Ignatius reconciliation and weekday Mass, St. Francis de Sales Saturday confession, and St. Cyprian office address. St. Jerome's Sunday times remain disputed between the parish site and the Archdiocese listing, and the record says so. No rate limiting was seen. Budget was not exhausted.
